freeze_method: inspect.signature() on the installed pyreadstat 1.3.6 in the PHASE 1 isolated environment. Defaults below are OBSERVED from the installed build, not recalled.

data_pass.precondition: reached only when compatibility_full_read is True, i.e. encoding is not None (:500)

chunked_pass.call: pyreadstat.read_file_in_chunks(reader, self._source_path, chunksize=rows_per_chunk, encoding=self._encoding, apply_value_formats=False, user_missing=True)
chunked_pass.reachability: taken only when self._frame is None, i.e. on the encoding=None lane (:147-149)

no_unidentified_default_governs_C4.assertion: Every pyreadstat parameter that reaches a C4 read is now either explicitly passed by the repository or listed below with its observed default and its measured effect on this anchor.

formats_as_category.explanation: Governs whether value-labelled variables are returned as pandas Categorical rather than plain values. The repository never passes it, so it inherits True.
formats_as_category.why_the_C3_court_still_passes: The C4 decoder also passes apply_value_formats=False on every call, which suppresses value-label application to cell text. With value formats suppressed, the categorical path does not alter cell values on this build. This is an EMPIRICAL observation on pyreadstat 1.3.6 with pandas 2.3.3, verified by the clean 55/55 court and by probe G01-1, NOT a repository guarantee.
formats_as_category.binding: frozen at True for pyreadstat 1.3.6 + pandas 2.3.3 on this anchor

formats_as_ordered_category.explanation: Would make any categorical ORDERED rather than plain. Inert while formats_as_category produces no categories.

dates_as_pandas_datetime.explanation: This is the single option that decides whether a SAV date variable arrives as a built-in datetime.date/datetime.datetime or as a pandas datetime64 column. It directly governs the D02 opaque carrier. The repository never passes it.
dates_as_pandas_datetime.measured_effect_on_this_anchor: D02-5 measured that a synthetic SAV DATE variable arrives as built-in datetime.date with pandas dtype 'object', NOT as a pandas datetime64 column. The accepted decoder converts it to R5OpaqueValue('python.datetime.date@1', payload b'\x06.\x0a\x0e').
dates_as_pandas_datetime.binding: frozen at False; MUST remain False for the accepted D02 date@1 carrier to be what O1-C04 expects

disable_datetime_conversion.explanation: The second date-lane control. Never passed by the repository.

row_limit.explanation: 0 means no limit; the C4 read economy is enforced by selecting columns/operations upstream, not by row_limit.

output_format.explanation: None selects the default dict-of-DataFrame output.

usecols.explanation: None reads all columns. Column restriction for C4 is applied by the callers that use read_sav directly, not by the decoder.
usecols.binding: frozen at None for the decoder path

extra_date_formats.explanation: No extra date format strings are supplied, so only SPSS built-in date formats are honoured.

ordered_category_behaviour.finding: formats_as_ordered_category defaults to False, so any categorical produced via formats_as_category=True is UNORDERED on this build.
ordered_category_behaviour.consequence: No ordered categorical can arise on the C4 read path under the frozen configuration. Any future change to this pair would alter cell typing and must be re-qualified.
ordered_category_behaviour.verified_by: probe G01-1 and the clean 55/55 authoritative court

chunksize.explanation: The repository overrides it with rows_per_chunk = max(1, batch_size // max(1, len(variables))), so the default 100000 is never inherited on the chunked lane. The KWARG NAME chunksize itself is a pyreadstat API-surface dependency and is frozen.
chunksize.binding: explicitly computed by the repository; default never inherited

frozen_reader_contract_for_C4.applies_to: every C4 governed SAV and DTA source read

valid_only_for.statement: These defaults are properties of the installed pyreadstat build. Any pyreadstat or pandas version change voids this freeze and requires re-qualification of PHASE 3 and PHASE 4.

material_finding_carried_to_O1_C05_and_O.finding: DTA-3 in 04_SYNTHETIC_READER_PROBES.json measures that the physical-metadata digest is READER-LANE BOUND, not source-only.
material_finding_carried_to_O1_C05_and_O.why: reader_configuration — which carries encoding and authority_status — is inside the physical-metadata digest payload. The source bytes are identical across both lanes; only the reader lane differs.
material_finding_carried_to_O1_C05_and_O.consequence: A frozen physical-metadata digest is valid ONLY for its exact reader lane. The source warrant under O1-C06 must bind the reader lane together with the source identity, not the source identity alone.
material_finding_carried_to_O1_C05_and_O.repeat_stability: Decode IS repeatable: two consecutive decodes of the same synthetic source in the same lane produced bit-identical digests and identical row counts.
